messages:
alex: Heads-up — noticed a lot of small GPU nodes sitting at ~10-20% and CA is not consolidating. Pod packing looks fragmented across AZs. Any quick wins before we roll an infra change?

maria: can you paste the CA flags currently running? this smells like `binpack` expander + nodegroup weights.

alex: here’s the CA args from prod (redacted):
```
--expander=binpack
--balance-similar-node-groups=true
--scale-down-unneeded-time=5m
--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.5
--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=true
--max-empty-bulk-delete=20
```

ken: that `skip-nodes-with-local-storage=true` will stop CA from deleting GPUs if any local scratch PV exists, even tiny files. for GPU pools we usually set false so CA can consolidate.

sanjay: +1. also `binpack` sometimes overfits to CPU histograms and leaves small GPU shards. try `--expander=least-wasteful` or `--expander=priority` with weights for gpu nodegroups.

joanne: caution: lowering `scale-down-unneeded-time` too much causes churn. we had bad flapping when it was 2m. set to 10m at least, maybe 15m for GPU pools.

maria: proposed experiment flags for staging:
```
--expander=least-wasteful
--balance-similar-node-groups=true
--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m
--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.6
--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false
--max-empty-bulk-delete=5
```

alex: ps: current node list snapshot (trimmed):
```
NAME                      STATUS   ROLES    AGE    CPU%   MEM%
gpu-eu-west-1a-02         Ready    <none>   2d     12%    28%
gpu-eu-west-1b-03         Ready    <none>   1d     9%     22%
gpu-eu-west-1c-01         Ready    <none>   6h     15%    30%
```

infra-bot: [23:07] cluster-autoscaler: scale-down candidates -> gpu-eu-west-1b-03 (unused pods: 0; allocatable GPU:1)

sanjay: another knob — `--max-node-provision-time` and `--max-empty-bulk-delete` tuned down avoids over-eager mass deletions that trigger preemptible churn. also consider `--node-group-auto-discovery` labels to control which groups CA considers.

ken: for cost-aware scheduling we added label `redwood.priority/gpu=0.8` on denser instance types. with `priority` expander you can factor that in. weight map: low-cost dense nodes get lower weight => prefer them.

maria: we should also enable `--balance-similar-node-groups` (already true) and `--expander=least-wasteful` in prod in a canary stanza for one cluster for 24h. monitor pod evictions, p95 latency, and preemptible reclaim rate.

joanne: scheduling the canary: deploy to staging now, then eu-west canary tomorrow 02:00 UTC, rollback if `scale_events > 10` in 30m window or `node_flap_rate` spikes. I'll add to the runbook.

alex: ok will flip in staging. leaving `max-empty-bulk-delete=5` to be safe.

deploy-bot: applied new CA flags to `staging` at 23:10 — job 3472.

alex: quick note — add a check to our alerts: if `scale_down_actions > scale_up_actions` for 1h then pause further scale-downs and page. had a case where CA consolidated then OOMed pods because of binpack mismatch.

sanjay: good call. also add a per-nodegroup metric `gpu_utilization_by_pod_type` so we don't treat training clusters like low-latency inference pools.

maria: sgtm. next steps: run staging 24h, collect packing fragmentation metric (percent of GPU capacity with <25% utilization), then canary to eu-west. I'll own the dashboard. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

alex: :thumbsup: thanks all, will watch staging and report back in this thread.
